did_you_know.text: Did you know? David looks for someone from the house of Saul to whom he can show kindness, saying that he wants to do so for Jonathan’s sake.
Did you know? Ziba is described as a servant who belonged to the house of Saul, and David summons him to find out whether any descendant of Saul’s family remains.
Did you know? David calls the kindness he wants to show “the kindness of God”—an expression emphasizing the greatness and special nature of this kindness.
Did you know? Ziba tells the king about Mephibosheth, Jonathan’s son, and says that he is staying at the house of Machir son of Ammiel in Lo-debar.
Did you know? David is not satisfied with the information he receives; instead, he sends for Mephibosheth himself from the house of Machir son of Ammiel.
Did you know? Mephibosheth, Jonathan’s son and Saul’s grandson, comes before David, falls facedown, and bows to him.
Did you know? David reassures Mephibosheth and promises him two things: to restore to him all the land that belonged to his father Saul, and to let him always eat at the king’s table.
Did you know? Mephibosheth responds with great humility, describing himself as “a dead dog,” an expression of his sense of worthlessness in light of David’s kindness.
Did you know? David orders that everything that belonged to Saul and his household be given to Mephibosheth, and he assigns Ziba responsibility for managing the property.

Did you know? Ziba, his sons, and his servants are required to work the land and bring in its produce so that Mephibosheth will have food; nevertheless, Mephibosheth himself will always eat at the king’s table.
